plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large daisy-like flower heads made of a dark central disc surrounded by bright yellow ray petals. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is widely grown for seeds, oil, and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated worldwide, especially in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west each day (heliotropism), but mature flowers stop moving and face east, which helps warm them and attract pollinators.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower forming tall stems topped with plume-like clusters of tiny golden flowers. It thrives in meadows, roadsides, and open fields and is an important late-season nectar source for bees, butterflies, and other pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to North America, from eastern Canada through the northern and central United States; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and spread by insects; the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time.

plants.name: Lespedeza thunbergii
plants.description: A graceful arching shrub-like perennial that produces cascading sprays of small pea-shaped magenta-pink flowers. It is beloved in Japanese gardens and temples, where its flowing branches create a fountain effect in late summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to early autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Hagi is one of the Seven Flowers of Autumn (Aki no Nanakusa) in Japan and is mentioned in more poems in the ancient Man'yoshu anthology than any other plant.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or large shrub with feathery blue-green foliage and fluffy, fragrant, ball-shaped golden flower clusters. In Australia it flowers at the end of winter, brightening bushland and gardens as spring approaches.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including South Australia, Victoria, New South Wales, and the ACT
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring, right after the blooming begins in earnest.
